identity.version: IHP SG13G2 Layout Rules Rev 2.1 (2024-12-19) / interposer_tech_default v1.2
identity.provenance: Transcribed from the open IHP-derived interposer PDK (Apache-2.0). GDS layer/datatype from interposer/libs.tech/klayout/tech/intm4tm2.lyt <symbols> and intm4tm2.map; per-layer width/spacing and via cut/enclosure from interposer/libs.tech/klayout/tech/drc/rule_decks/interposer_tech_default.json (transcribed at v1.2, unchanged through v1.7) cross-checked against decks 5_17_metaln, 5_20_via4, 5_21_topvia1, 5_24_topvia2; connectivity from intm4tm2.lyt <connection>. Attachment references interconnect_pdk fab_anchor ihp_cupillar_anchor; no bump geometry copied. No kit files ingested beyond these open, Apache-licensed sources. The pad exit length routability.pad_exit_um is Pad_fR (7.00) of the same rules file as the ADK pins it (intm4tm2 0.1.0, interposer_tech_default.json v1.7), the value rule Pad.fR of 6_9_pad.drc reads.
identity.description: IHP SG13G2 IntM4TM2 2.5D interposer routing technology: 4 backend metals (Metal4, Metal5, TopMetal1, TopMetal2) and 3 vias (Via4, TopVia1, TopVia2). Multi-layer RDL variant: routability.route_layers selects the grt/drt two-layer detailed router on TopMetal1 (met3) + TopMetal2 (met4). Identical to ihp_sg13g2_intm4tm2 except route_layers; kept in sync by test_rdl2_variant_is_golden_plus_route_layers.

inloop_drc.parity_scope: Assembly rules are read from adk/config/rule_params.json, never copied here. docs/limits.md says which stage checks each rule.
inloop_drc.notes: In-loop DRC built from this contract is a geometric pre-filter only, never signoff.

notes: pitch_um for every layer is DERIVED = min_width + min_spacing. IHP interposer_tech_default.json defines NO routing pitch; the only 'pitch' in the IHP DRC tree is Cu-pillar/bump pitch (Padc_e in 6_9_copperpillar.drc), a different (bump) axis.
preferred_direction is an ENGINE routing convention (alternating HORIZONTAL/VERTICAL bottom->top), NOT an IHP fab rule; no routing direction is stated in any IHP source.
routability.pin_layers (met4 = TopMetal2, where Cu-pillar bump pads are presented) and rc_layer (met2) are ENGINE choices for the 2.5D bump-RDL use case, not IHP fab rules.

Via4 enclosure is symmetric 0.005/0.005: 5_20_via4.drc rule V4.c (Metal4, bottom) and V4.c2 (Metal5, top) both use Vn_c=0.005. Vn_c1=0.05 is present in interposer_tech_default.json but is UNUSED by 5_20_via4.drc, so it is deliberately NOT transcribed as the top enclosure.

No parasitics (resistance/capacitance) or physical stack are included: IHP provides none in the consolidated routing sources. EM/SI/parasitic values come from Palace/measurement (SI addendum), not from fab data.

manufacturing_grid_um = 0.005 is the fab manufacturing grid, transcribed from the interposer PDK deck libs.tech/klayout/tech/drc/rule_decks/3_1_offgrid.drc:36 (GRID = 5.nm; the header at line 26 reads 'Manufacturing grid: 5 nm => 0.005 um'). It is 5x dbu_um (0.001 um = intm4tm2.lyt <dbu>), so a LEF MANUFACTURINGGRID of 0.005 stays an exact multiple of the database unit. Interim literal transcription: the PDK ships no machine-readable grid projection this descriptor could reference by digest yet.

width_spacing is transcribed from the interposer PDK rules file interposer_tech_default.json v1.7 and the decks that read it. TopMetal2 has one row, TM2.bR of 5_25_topmetal2.drc. TopMetal1 has none: 5_22_topmetal1.drc checks only TM1.a and TM1.b. Metal4 and Metal5 leave the key out on purpose: Mn_e and Mn_f of 5_17_metaln.drc are width-dependent and not transcribed yet, so neither layer can carry a widened net.
Attachment is cupillar (UBM datatype /35). The solder-bump path (ihp_sbump_anchor, datatype /36) is available via interconnect_methods.json but not selected here.

max_width_um = 30.0 on Metal4, Metal5, TopMetal1 and TopMetal2 is Slt.c of interposer_tech_default.json v1.7 (key Slt_c, checked by 7_3_metalslits.drc): metal wider than 30 um needs slits. The deck does not forbid the width; the router draws no slits, so it refuses a net requirement wider than this until slitting exists.
